title: Federal Court Rules Trump-Era IRS Illegally Disclosed Taxpayer Data to Immigration Officials
snippet: A federal court has determined that the Internal Revenue Service breached federal tax privacy laws by sharing sensitive taxpayer information with immigration enforcement agencies during the Trump administration.
content:
A federal court has ruled that the Internal Revenue Service violated federal law during the Trump administration by unlawfully sharing confidential taxpayer information with federal immigration authorities.

Breach of Tax Privacy Laws

According to the ruling, the disclosures violated strict privacy protections enshrined in the Internal Revenue Code. Federal tax law generally prohibits the IRS from sharing personal tax returns and identifying details with other government agencies without explicit statutory authorization or a court order.

Civil rights advocates and privacy groups behind the legal challenge argued that the unauthorized data sharing severely undermined trust in the national tax system. The plaintiffs demonstrated that sharing sensitive information created a widespread chilling effect among immigrant communities, deterring noncitizens from obtaining Individual Taxpayer Identification Numbers (ITINs) and filing tax returns out of fear of executive enforcement actions.

Reaffirming Inter-Agency Boundaries

Legal experts and advocacy organizations hailed the decision as a major victory for civil liberties and statutory compliance. The ruling reinforces longstanding legal boundaries separating revenue collection from immigration policy, emphasizing that administrative agencies cannot bypass statutory privacy mandates to execute broader executive agendas.
